subject: Svenska
title: Word classes and sentence elements
sourceSummary: Nouns, verbs, adjectives and pronouns — and the difference between word class (what a word IS) and sentence element (what ROLE the word plays in a particular sentence).

questions.prompt: Which word in the sentence is a verb? "Den trötta hunden sprang snabbt hem."
questions.opener: A verb is the word that tells us what someone DOES or WHERE someone is.
questions.explanation: "Sprang" is the verb — it tells us what the dog does. "Trötta" is an adjective, "hunden" is a noun, and "snabbt" is an adverb.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adjective? "Hon köpte en dyr, blå cykel igår."
questions.opener: Adjectives describe how something IS or LOOKS — they are often inflected with -t or -a.
questions.explanation: "Dyr" describes the bike — it's an adjective (as is "blå"). "Köpte" is a verb, "igår" is an adverb, and "cykel" is a noun.

questions.prompt: Which word is a pronoun in the sentence? "Han gav henne boken innan han gick."
questions.opener: A pronoun replaces a noun instead of repeating the name.
questions.explanation: "Henne" stands in for a name (e.g. "Anna") — it's a pronoun. "Han" is also a pronoun, but "henne" was the answer being asked for here.

questions.prompt: Which word is the subject in the sentence? "Läraren rättade proven på kvällen."
questions.opener: The subject is the one PERFORMING the action — ask "who or what is doing this?"
questions.explanation: "Läraren" is the one performing the action (marking) — so it's the subject. Note that subject is a sentence element (a role), while "noun" is the word class the word belongs to.

questions.prompt: Which word is the predicate in the sentence? "Vi åt middag klockan sju."
questions.opener: The predicate is the verb in the sentence — the word that tells us what's happening.
questions.explanation: The predicate is always the verb (or verb chain) in the sentence — here "åt". "Vi" is the subject and "middag" is the object.

questions.prompt: Which word is the object in the sentence? "Pelle målade staketet i helgen."
questions.opener: The object is what the action is DIRECTED at — ask "what/who did he do it TO or WITH?"
questions.explanation: "Staketet" is what Pelle painted — the object receives the action. "Pelle" is the subject, "målade" is the predicate.

questions.prompt: Analyse the sentence: "Den nya eleven hälsade glatt på alla." State the word class of each word and the sentence element for the subject, predicate and object.
questions.opener: Go word by word. Then ask: who does it (subject), what do they do (predicate), and is there an object?
questions.answer: Den (definite article/pronoun), nya (adjective), eleven (noun, = subject), hälsade (verb, = predicate), glatt (adverb), på alla (preposition + pronoun, = object/complement).
steps: "Den" points to a definite noun — it's often counted as a determiner/pronoun.
"Eleven" is the one performing the action (greeting) — a noun as word class, subject as sentence element.
"Glatt" describes HOW the greeting happens — an adverb, not an adjective (adjectives describe nouns, adverbs describe verbs).
"På alla" tells us who the greeting is directed at — it functions as an object/complement to the predicate.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between word class and sentence element?
questions.opener: A word can have the same word class in every sentence, but a different sentence element depending on where it stands.
questions.answer: Word class is WHAT a word is in itself — noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, numeral. It never changes, no matter where in the sentence the word stands. Sentence element is what ROLE the word plays in that particular sentence — subject (the one doing something), predicate (the verb/action), object (the one receiving the action), or complement. Example: "hund" is always a noun (word class), but can be the subject in "Hunden skäller" and the object in "Jag ser hunden".
